title: Verification Result v1
description:
Deterministic, non-AI verification result for a candidate finding.

Per sl-competitor-methods-v1 (the agent/validator split) and sl-efficacy-gap-v1
(empty-data authorization differentials, no state-verification step): this is
the independent oracle that gates a finding before it can be marked confirmed.

Model-authored prose can NEVER mark a finding confirmed — only a deterministic
oracle (authorization differential, business-logic state read, SHA-256 canary,
or OOB callback) can produce outcome=verified.

Outcomes:
  - verified: the oracle's deterministic conditions were all met. The finding
    is real and impact was demonstrated.
  - disproved: the oracle's deterministic conditions showed the finding is
    false (a disconfirming control fired, or the cross-actor differential was
    absent, or the hash did not match). This is a TRUE NEGATIVE — the candidate
    finding was wrong.
  - insufficient_evidence: the oracle could not reach a deterministic
    verdict (missing evidence, tampered evidence, or the controlled victim
    marker was absent). The finding is neither confirmed nor refuted; the agent
    must gather more evidence. This is the ONLY outcome model prose can
    indirectly produce (by failing to supply the required evidence).

This schema is the single source of truth for the result shape. lib/verification.py
validates against it (manual layer always; jsonschema layer when available).
bin/lab-verify emits results conforming to it.

result_id.description: UUIDv4 identifying this verification result. Generated by the verifier.

finding_id.description:
Identifier of the candidate finding being verified. Must be non-empty.
The verifier does not assume any particular format; it is an opaque
reference for downstream correlation.

oracle.description:
Which deterministic oracle produced this result.
  - authorization: cross-actor response differential + controlled victim marker
    + verified ownership/workspace identity.
  - business_logic: separate post-action state read (not the mutation response).
  - sha256_canary: agent received only location + expected SHA-256; the canary
    value it retrieved must hash to the expected digest.
  - oob_callback: result accepted only from a captured callback record; the
    record must carry the collector-produced fields collector_id/timestamp/token
    as emitted by bin/lab-oob.

outcome.description:
Deterministic verdict.
  - verified: all oracle conditions met.
  - disproved: oracle showed the finding is false (true negative).
  - insufficient_evidence: oracle could not reach a deterministic verdict.

verified_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp the verification was run, e.g. 2026-08-03T12:34:56Z.

evidence.description:
Evidence references the oracle used to reach its verdict. Each entry is a
reference (path, label, or captured-record id) plus a kind. A verified result
MUST cite at least one piece of evidence; insufficient_evidence may have an
empty array (the evidence was missing — that is WHY the outcome is
insufficient). disproved results cite the disconfirming evidence here too.

ref.description:
Reference to the evidence: a filesystem path, a captured-record id, or a
label. Must be non-empty.

kind.description: What kind of evidence this is.

sha256.description:
Optional SHA-256 of the referenced evidence (hex, lowercase, 64 chars).
When present, the verifier confirms it matches the actual evidence content.
For tamper-resistance: a mismatch between cited sha256 and actual content
forces outcome=insufficient_evidence (never verified).

inline.description:
True when the evidence entry was synthesized by the oracle from the
caller's inline values (e.g. the cross-actor response body, the post-action
state read, the canary retrieved value) rather than captured to a file. The
ref of inline evidence is a placeholder label (e.g. "<cross_actor_response>"),
NOT a filesystem path -- replay consumers must never attempt to resolve it
as a path.

disconfirming_controls.description:
Disconfirming controls the oracle checked. A control is a check that, if it
fires, refutes the finding (forces disproved or blocks verified). For an
authorization oracle, the control is 'the no-credential request is denied
(401/403) — proving the endpoint is actually access-gated, so a cross-actor
200 is a real bypass, not an unauthenticated endpoint.' For business-logic, the
control is 'the state read confirms the mutation did NOT happen when the
precondition was violated.' For SHA-256 canary, the control is 'the retrieved
value hashes to the expected digest (any mismatch disproves).' For OOB, the
control is 'the callback record exists and was captured by the verifier (not
asserted by the agent), carrying the collector-produced fields
collector_id/timestamp/token as emitted by bin/lab-oob, with the record's
token bound exactly to the expected identifier.' Each entry documents whether the control passed
(refutes) or held (supports the finding).

name.description:
Short name of the control, e.g. 'no_credential_denied', 'state_read_confirms',
'canary_hash_matches', 'callback_record_captured'.

passed.description:
True = the control held (supports the finding / did not refute). False = the
control fired (refutes the finding / blocks verified). For a no-credential-denied
control: passed=true means the no-credential request WAS denied (the endpoint
is gated, so a cross-actor 200 is a real bypass). passed=false means the
no-credential request succeeded too (the endpoint is ungated — not a bypass).

detail.description:
Short human-readable explanation of what the control checked and the observed
result. Must be non-empty.
examples: no-credential GET /workspaces/123 returned 401 — endpoint is access-gated
retrieved canary SHA-256 matches expected digest

reason.description:
Short deterministic reason for the outcome. For verified: which oracle conditions
were met. For disproved: which control fired. For insufficient_evidence: what
was missing. Optional but recommended.
examples: cross-actor response contained victim marker and ownership verified; no-credential control denied
canary hash mismatch: expected a..e got b..f

target.description:
Target host or URL the candidate finding concerns. Optional — included for
audit correlation. Refused if it is out of scope (the verifier never contacts
live targets, but it records the target for the audit log).

engagement.description:
Engagement name the candidate finding belongs to. Optional — included for
audit correlation.

disconfirming_controls.name: no_credential_denied
disconfirming_controls.detail: no-credential GET returned 401 — endpoint is access-gated

disconfirming_controls.name: victim_marker_present
disconfirming_controls.detail: cross-actor response contained the controlled victim marker

disconfirming_controls.name: ownership_verified
disconfirming_controls.detail: response owner_user_id matches victim workspace, not attacker

examples.reason: cross-actor response contained victim marker and ownership verified; no-credential control denied

disconfirming_controls.name: canary_hash_matches
disconfirming_controls.detail: retrieved value SHA-256 e3b0...b855 != expected ba78...15ad

examples.reason: canary hash mismatch: retrieved value does not hash to the expected digest
